issues.legal_issue: Disputes relating to wakf property within the special statutory regime must be brought before the Wakf Tribunal in the first instance rather than directly before a civil court or the High Court.
material_facts: The dispute concerned property constituted as a wakf estate and questions about its division under the wakf deed and the application of the statutory regime to a portion of that property.
The proceeding was commenced after the statutory regime came into force.
The dispute was not an eviction dispute.
issues.conclusion: The Wakf Tribunal had jurisdiction in the first instance, and the parties could not bring this dispute directly before the civil court or the High Court; the High Court judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 83(1) of the Wakf Act, 1995 gives the Tribunal jurisdiction to determine any dispute, question or other matter relating to a wakf or wakf property, and section 84 supports that broad jurisdiction. Section 83(9) provides for recourse to the High Court after the Tribunal's decision. Section 83(5) gives the Tribunal civil-court powers, including powers to grant and enforce temporary injunctions. The Court applied the principle that a special statutory forum displaces recourse to the general forum, relying on Justice G.P. Singh's Principles of Statutory Interpretation and Chief Engineer, Hydel Project v. Ravinder Nath. It distinguished Ramesh Gobindram v. Sugra Humayun Mirza Wakf because that case concerned eviction proceedings.

rule.if: wakf_related_proceeding and property_is_wakf_property and special_forum_regime_applies and not eviction_dispute

predicates.wakf_related_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to resolve a dispute, question or other matter relating to a wakf or wakf property.
predicates.property_is_wakf_property: The property involved in the dispute is treated as wakf property.
predicates.special_forum_regime_applies: The proceeding falls within the operation of the special statutory regime that assigns such matters to a Tribunal.
predicates.eviction_dispute: The proceeding concerns eviction from property.
predicates.wakf_tribunal_is_first_instance_forum: The Wakf Tribunal is the forum that must be approached first to determine the dispute.

issues.definition: When a proceeding within the special forum regime concerns wakf property and is not an eviction dispute, the Tribunal is the first forum for resolving it.

issues.legal_issue: The Wakf Tribunal may determine a dispute relating to a wakf or wakf property even when no order has previously been made under the governing statute.
material_facts: The Court considered whether Tribunal jurisdiction depended on a prior order made under the statute.
The dispute concerned a wakf and its property, and the statutory provisions addressed the determination of disputes and other matters relating to wakfs or wakf property.
issues.conclusion: A party may approach the Wakf Tribunal to determine a dispute relating to a wakf or wakf property even if no order has been passed under the statute.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 83(1) and 84 of the Wakf Act, 1995 independently confer jurisdiction to determine any dispute, question or other matter relating to a wakf or wakf property. That jurisdiction is not confined to reviewing the correctness of an order under section 83(2), and no prior statutory order is required.

predicates.wakf_related_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to resolve a dispute, question or other matter relating to a wakf or wakf property.
predicates.no_prior_order_under_special_law: No order has previously been made under the special law concerning the dispute.
predicates.tribunal_can_be_approached_without_prior: The party may seek the Tribunal's determination without first obtaining an order under the special law.

issues.definition: If a proceeding concerns a wakf or wakf property and no prior order has been made under the special law, the Tribunal may still be approached to determine the matter.

issues.legal_issue: The special statutory regime does not govern wakf proceedings that were commenced before that regime came into force.
material_facts: The Court stated that proceedings commenced before the Wakf Act, 1995 came into force are not governed by that Act.
The proceeding in this case was commenced in 1999, after the Act came into force.
issues.conclusion: The pre-commencement exception did not apply to this proceeding; the Court recognized that proceedings begun before the Act came into force are not governed by it.
issues.legal_principle: Relying on Sardar Khan v. Syed Najmul Hasan (Seth), the Court held that the Wakf Act, 1995 does not apply to suits, appeals, revisions or other proceedings commenced before it came into force on 1 January 1996.

predicates.wakf_related_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to resolve a dispute, question or other matter relating to a wakf or wakf property.
predicates.proceeding_started_before_special_regime: The proceeding was commenced before the special statutory regime came into force.
predicates.special_regime_does_not_govern_proceedin: The special statutory regime does not apply to the proceeding.

issues.definition: A proceeding relating to a wakf or wakf property is outside the special regime when it began before that regime came into force.
